gemini_advisory.farmer_plain_language_summary: We have combined your on-farm measurements—like your specific soil compaction and rain gauge data—with NASA's satellite view of your field. Your silt loam soil is currently in decent shape, but the moderate plowpan (225 PSI) is a bottleneck for root growth. We have mapped out five ways to manage your 25-hectare parcel over the next three years, balancing your need for cash flow against the long-term health of your dirt.

strategies_breakdown.benefits_plain_words: Highest cash profit and significant savings on fertilizer costs thanks to the nitrogen-fixing power of alfalfa.
strategies_breakdown.drawbacks_plain_words: Increases soil compaction over time; you will need to manage the hardpan carefully.
strategies_breakdown.risks_taken: Risk of worsening the existing plowpan due to heavy equipment passes.
strategies_breakdown.expected_rewards: Strongest financial return while still getting a boost from natural nitrogen.
strategies_breakdown.three_year_action_overview: Year 1: Plant Grain Sorghum. Year 2: Establish Alfalfa to fix nitrogen. Year 3: Return to Grain Sorghum, utilizing the nitrogen left by the alfalfa.

strategies_breakdown.benefits_plain_words: Best for building your soil's 'sponge' and breaking up the hardpan to allow deeper root growth.
strategies_breakdown.drawbacks_plain_words: Very low immediate cash profit; requires high labor and more field passes.
strategies_breakdown.risks_taken: Financial risk due to low market returns compared to high operational costs.
strategies_breakdown.expected_rewards: A healthier, more resilient field that will be easier to work in the long run.
strategies_breakdown.three_year_action_overview: Year 1: Plant Winter Wheat. Year 2: Seed Alfalfa. Year 3: Maintain Alfalfa to maximize soil structure and nitrogen fixation.

strategies_breakdown.benefits_plain_words: Saves you time and fuel with fewer trips across the field; keeps cash flow steady.
strategies_breakdown.drawbacks_plain_words: Accelerates soil compaction; your soil will become tighter and harder to work.
strategies_breakdown.risks_taken: High risk of creating a severe hardpan that will eventually hurt your yields.
strategies_breakdown.expected_rewards: High ROI and low labor stress in the short term.
strategies_breakdown.three_year_action_overview: Year 1: Plant Soybeans. Year 2: Plant Grain Sorghum. Year 3: Plant Grain Sorghum again.

strategies_breakdown.benefits_plain_words: Best bang for your buck; keeps your equipment costs low and profit margins high.
strategies_breakdown.drawbacks_plain_words: Does little to improve soil structure; you are essentially mining the soil for profit.
strategies_breakdown.risks_taken: Compaction risk is high; you are trading long-term soil health for immediate cash.
strategies_breakdown.expected_rewards: Excellent return on your investment capital.
strategies_breakdown.three_year_action_overview: Year 1: Plant Grain Sorghum. Year 2: Plant Soybeans. Year 3: Return to Grain Sorghum.

strategies_breakdown.benefits_plain_words: Safest bet against bad weather or market swings; keeps your soil loose and healthy.
strategies_breakdown.drawbacks_plain_words: High labor requirement and more field passes; lower total profit.
strategies_breakdown.risks_taken: Accepting lower profit in exchange for a very stable, low-risk farming system.
strategies_breakdown.expected_rewards: Peace of mind and a significant improvement in soil structure.
strategies_breakdown.three_year_action_overview: Year 1: Establish Alfalfa. Year 2: Plant Grain Sorghum. Year 3: Re-establish Alfalfa.

gemini_advisory.three_year_operational_overview: Year 1 focuses on establishment and soil preparation. Year 2 is the transition phase where you manage the nitrogen legacy of the previous crop. Year 3 is the harvest and consolidation phase, where you will see the cumulative effects of your chosen rotation on soil structure and compaction.
gemini_advisory.risk_vs_reward_comparison: The 'Most Income' and 'Highest ROI' plans prioritize your wallet today but risk 'concrete-like' soil compaction tomorrow. Conversely, the 'Best Soil Health' and 'Least Crop Loss' plans prioritize the long-term health of your land, acting like an insurance policy against future crop failure, though they require more sweat equity and offer smaller immediate paychecks.
gemini_advisory.farmer_decision_guide: Choose 'Most Income' if you need cash now and have the equipment to manage compaction. Choose 'Best Soil Health' if your primary goal is to pass on a better field to the next generation. Choose 'Least Effort' if labor is your biggest constraint. Choose 'Least Crop Loss' if you are worried about volatile weather and want the most stable, low-risk system.
ground_truth_field_checklist: Check the depth of the plowpan with a probe every spring.
Monitor rainfall vs. your soil moisture probe to see how well your soil holds water.
Check for signs of water runoff on the 2.8% slope after heavy rains.
Test soil nitrogen levels after alfalfa cycles to adjust your fertilizer bill.
gemini_advisory.executive_summary: Your field is currently at a crossroads. While you have decent soil organic matter, the moderate plowpan is a ticking clock. The simulation shows that you can either maximize your short-term profit at the cost of soil structure or invest in soil health to ensure long-term stability. The 'Most Income' strategy offers the best balance for a commercial operation, while 'Least Crop Loss' is the best choice for risk-averse management.
gemini_advisory.parcel_climate_context: Your field faces a high evaporative demand (1200mm), meaning the sun and wind are constantly trying to dry out your soil. With only 82.5mm of measured rainfall, your crop success depends entirely on how well your soil holds onto that moisture. Your silt loam texture is a great asset, but it needs organic matter to act as a sponge to keep that water available for your roots.
gemini_advisory.strategy_tradeoff_matrix: The strategies create a clear divide: High-profit strategies (Most Income, Highest ROI) rely on intensive cropping that degrades soil structure. Soil-building strategies (Best Soil Health, Least Crop Loss) trade immediate cash for better water retention and lower compaction, but they demand more labor and time.
gemini_advisory.year_by_year_soil_transformation: Year 1 starts with your current 1.94% organic matter and 225 PSI compaction. In high-intensity rotations, compaction will climb toward 300+ PSI by Year 3. In soil-building rotations, you will see the compaction level off or drop, and your soil's ability to hold water will improve as the organic sponge grows.
gemini_advisory.extreme_event_resilience_playbook: For drought: Prioritize the 'Best Soil Health' rotation to increase water holding. For heatwaves: Ensure your soil is covered to reduce evaporation. For heavy downpours: Use the 'Least Crop Loss' rotation to keep roots in the ground and prevent erosion on your 2.8% slope. For frost: Ensure your winter wheat is well-established in the fall.
